updates.name: Jennifer Dorton
updates.bio: Joined SECOORA in 2017 as manager of its Regional Coastal Ocean Observing System, charged with the updated regional observing plan, data management and communications, and coordinating the association's investigators. Earlier she spent over 13 years leading grant-funded work at UNC Wilmington, as a PI on its Coastal Ocean Research and Monitoring Program and lead PI on the Marine Weather Portal.
updates.current_affiliation: Southeast Coastal Ocean Observing Regional Association (SECOORA)
updates.notes: Bio from the SECOORA announcement of 2017-08-23 (her RCOOS Manager hire); current title Deputy Director from secoora.org/about/contact/ (fetched 200). Existing ORCID 0009-0001-2786-7582 re-checked on pub.orcid.org: name Jennifer Dorton, employment SECOORA, Deputy Director, 2017-present; no change. No individual profile page found, so homepage_url left null. No Google Scholar link on any fetched page.

updates.name: Trika Gerard
updates.bio: Deputy Director for Science and Operations in the NOAA Southeast Fisheries Science Center directorate. A marine ecologist at the Center since 2007, she studies early life stages of coral reef and highly migratory fishes in the Gulf and Caribbean, covering larval transport, food webs, otolith microstructure and recruitment connectivity, and leads a RESTORE-funded study of bluefin tuna larval habitat.
updates.research_interests: larval fish ecology; coral reef and highly migratory fishes; larval distribution and transport; otolith microstructure; recruitment connectivity; bluefin tuna larval trophic ecology

updates.current_affiliation: NOAA Fisheries Southeast Fisheries Science Center

updates.name: Megan Medina
updates.bio: Ecologist whose background is in the biodiversity and composition of fisheries, working for SCCOOS, the IOOS regional association for Southern California, at Scripps Institution of Oceanography. As program coordinator she builds partnerships with decision-makers, scientists and stakeholders to co-develop value-added products for users, after research-assistant work for NOAA's Office of National Marine Sanctuaries on Florida Keys reef fish biodiversity.
updates.current_affiliation: Southern California Coastal Ocean Observing System, Scripps Institution of Oceanography, UC San Diego
updates.notes: Identity: Scripps profile (scripps.ucsd.edu/profiles/memedina, 200) describes her as SCCOOS Program Coordinator; SCCOOS committee page (sccoos.org/?p=16021 -> sccoos.org/committee/, 200) lists 'Megan Medina, SCCOOS Deputy Director'. ORCID 0000-0001-5865-3504 found by ORCID registry search: pub.orcid.org record name Megan Medina, employment University of California San Diego, Scripps Institution of Oceanography (2017-present); its education (University of South Florida, University of Maryland) also matches the degrees on the Scripps profile. updates.name: Krisa Arzayus
updates.bio: Deputy director of NOAA's U.S. Integrated Ocean Observing System office, managing its strategic planning and implementation, including budget and staffing, with regional and national partners. Trained in chemistry, with a marine science PhD from William & Mary, she started at NOAA as a Knauss Sea Grant Fellow and later led data stewardship and oceanographic science units at NODC and NCEI.
updates.current_title: Acting Director (Federal), U.S. IOOS Program Office
updates.current_affiliation: NOAA National Ocean Service, U.S. Integrated Ocean Observing System Office
updates.notes: Bio from the 2023 NOS career profile (titled Deputy Director). The IOOS February 2026 newsletter (ioos.noaa.gov/?p=24296, 200) says she moved into the acting Director role on 2026-01-26 after Jeffrey Payne retired; the program office page lists her as Acting Director (Federal). updates.name: Daniel B. Fagre
updates.bio: USGS research ecologist with the Northern Rocky Mountain Science Center, based at its Glacier Field Station in Glacier National Park. In 2018 he headed the USGS mountain-ecosystems climate change project and the Benchmark Glacier Program, studying glaciers, avalanches, alpine plants, snow chemistry and paleoclimates, and won the USGS Shoemaker award for science communication.
updates.research_interests: climate change in mountain ecosystems; glacier monitoring; snow avalanches; alpine vegetation; snow chemistry; paleoclimates; bioregional ecosystem dynamics
updates.evidence: Research Ecologist Dan Fagre is the recipient of the 2017 Eugene M. Shoemaker Award

updates.name: Marc Macias-Fauria
updates.bio: Professor of Physical Geography at the Scott Polar Research Institute, University of Cambridge, leading the Biogeosciences group. Research examines how physical and biological components of the Earth system interact in Arctic and alpine regions, including links among vegetation, large herbivores and climate and the influence of sea ice on Arctic life, drawing on remote sensing, observations and palaeo-ecological records.
updates.research_interests: Arctic and alpine biogeosciences; vegetation-herbivore-climate interactions; sea-ice effects on Arctic biota; remote sensing of Arctic greening and browning; long-term Arctic biodiversity and palaeoecology
updates.current_affiliation: Scott Polar Research Institute and Department of Geography, University of Cambridge
